explain: _meminī_ takes the genitive of the person remembered. The genitive of _tū_ is _tuī_.
distractors: _tibi_ is dative (“to you”). _meminī_ takes the genitive: _tuī_.
_tū_ is the nominative “you” (the one doing). What you remember is genitive: _tuī_.

explain: What you remember goes in the genitive: _patris_, genitive singular of _pater_.
distractors: _pater_ is nominative. What you remember is genitive: _patris_.
_patrum_ is genitive plural (“of fathers”). One father: _patris_.
_amīcīs_ is dative or ablative. _meminī_ takes the genitive: _amīcōrum_.
_amīcī_ is genitive singular: “I remember a friend”. For “friends”: _amīcōrum_.
_amīcus_ is nominative. What you remember is genitive: _amīcōrum_.
_patriīs_ is dative or ablative plural. _meminī_ takes the genitive: _patriae_.
_patria_ is nominative (or ablative). What you remember is genitive: _patriae_.
_patriārum_ is genitive plural (“of homelands”). One homeland: _patriae_.

explain: _diēs_ is a fifth-declension noun (masculine here), so _bonōrum_ agrees with it: genitive plural _diērum bonōrum_.
distractors: _diēbus bonīs_ is dative or ablative. _meminī_ takes the genitive: _diērum bonōrum_.
_bonārum_ is feminine. _diēs_ is masculine here, so _bonōrum_.
_diēī bonī_ is genitive singular (“of the good day”). For “days”: _diērum bonōrum_.

explain: _memor_ (mindful) takes the genitive of what you are mindful of: _tuī_.
distractors: _tuus_ means “your” (an adjective), not “of you”. The genitive pronoun is _tuī_.
_nōs_ is nominative or accusative. After _memor_: genitive, _nostrī_.
_nōbīs_ is dative or ablative. After _memor_: genitive, _nostrī_.

en: I am mindful of you all.
explain: _vestrī_ is the genitive of _vōs_ (you, several people).
distractors: _vōs_ is nominative or accusative. After _memor_: genitive, _vestrī_.
_vōbīs_ is dative or ablative. After _memor_: genitive, _vestrī_.
_tuī_ is “of you” (one person). For several people: _vestrī_.
